items.title: Victoria's election day arrives, as state appears poised to dump Labor
paras: The battle between Jess Wilson and Ben Carroll culminates today. ( ABC News: Danielle Bonica )
Election day has finally arrived in Victoria after a campaign marked by Labor's plummeting polling and a controversial last-minute policy dump from the Coalition.
Around half the state's 4.7 million eligible voters have already cast their ballots via postal votes and at early voting centres.
The remainder will head to polling booths today, in an election widely expected to bring about a change of government after 12 years of Labor.
The Coalition's campaign has not been without controversy, with Liberal leader Jess Wilson on the defensive after a last-minute reveal of planned privatisation and kinder cuts.
The Coalition's path to victory, which relies on picking up more than a dozen new seats, could also be complicated by the rise in popularity of One Nation.
Jess Wilson has been trying to clean up the Liberal Party's image after years of internal division. ( ABC News: Antonia O'Flaherty )
The past four years have involved difficult chapters for both Labor and the Liberals, with three leadership changes each since Daniel Andrews and Matthew Guy led their parties to the 2022 election.
Andrews resigned from politics in 2023, handing Labor leadership and premier's job to Jacinta Allan.
Then as Labor's popularity plummeted amid Big Build corruption allegations and a controversial change to the emergency services levy, Ms Allan was backed into resigning this July.
Ben Carroll seized the premiership from Jacinta Allan amid concerns over Big Build corruption. ( AAP: Joel Carrett )
After earlier denying he would challenge Allan, then-deputy premier Ben Carroll became the leader after what has been described as a chaotic party room meeting.
The Liberal Party has rolled out three leaders since the last election — Matthew Guy, Brad Battin and finally Jess Wilson.
But the Liberals' leadership challenges faded firmly into the past as the party surged ahead in the polls on the back of the spate of home invasions, car thefts, machete attacks and firebombings.

The Wilson-led opposition continued on a platform of law and order throughout the year, which played out as an extended election campaign, well in excess of the traditional six-week timeframes of the past.
However Carroll, Wilson, One Nation's Warren Pickering and the Greens' Ellen Sandell did front a televised leaders forum, discussing questions from the audience.
Despite calling a royal commission into the Big Build allegations, Carroll has also been weighed down by Victoria's soaring debt and two controversial leaders during Labor's years in government.
And while polling continues to suggest a Wilson-led Coalition will win today's election, the results are not expected to be all rosy.
Earlier predictions of One Nation's success have been tempered by more recent opinion polls that now have Pauline Hanson's party trailing the Coalition by some way.
Pauline Hanson and Warren Pickering ahead of the race to pick up seats in the Victorian election. ( ABC News )
It has been a bumpy campaign for the party with one candidate dumped over social media posts that praised Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler .
Another stepped down after anti-Muslim rhetoric and for making highly sexualised remarks including that seeking consent was "cringe".
Anti-violence campaigners accused yet another of making misogynistic comments on a video featuring former AFL player Dustin Martin.
Even party leader Warren Pickering had to front the media in September, admitting to a history of drug use and drink driving when he was younger , after allegations were aired by a former partner.
Still, One Nation is expected to attract more than 20 per cent of the primary vote.
Progressive voters are looking elsewhere, which has created hope among the Victorian Greens.
Ellen Sandell (left) used colourful stunts to keep the Greens campaign focused on the party's traditional strengths of environmental advocacy and social justice. ( ABC News )
The party is looking to retain its seats in Melbourne, Richmond and Brunswick, and is optimistic about taking back Northcote and Prahran.
The Greens also have their eyes on Footscray, Pascoe Vale, and possibly Preston and Albert Park.
But Victorian Greens leader Ellen Sandell said the party was facing some tough hurdles.
"We know that Greens seats are actually always incredibly close," she said.

"This time, in particular, in order for the Greens to win a seat, we essentially have to get more votes than Labor, Liberal, One Nation combined because of the preference deals [they] have done with each other."
As Victoria votes, the ABC will have comprehensive coverage across our radio, television and online platforms.
Our live blog will keep you across all the latest developments throughout the day, with results analysis from state political reporter Rachel Eddie .
Election night coverage kicks off at 6pm on ABC TV, ABC News Channel, and streaming on iview .
The program will be simulcast on 774 ABC Melbourne and across all ABC Regional Victorian radio stations. Tune in online using the ABC Listen app.

Hosts David Speers and Patricia Karvelas will be joined by chief elections and data analyst Casey Briggs , state political reporter Richard Willingham and 774 ABC Melbourne Mornings presenter Raf Epstein to bring you fast, accurate and reliable analysis of the results.
Keep an eye on the ABC's social media platforms for highlights from the day's coverage, and explore more Victorian election news coverage and analysis on our website.

items.title: Zelenskyy says Trump's relationship with Putin like being friends with Hitler
paras: Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has voiced frustration at how the US is handling peace negotiations with Russia. ( BBC News )
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has criticised Donald Trump's "strange" relationship with Russia's Vladimir Putin who he likened to Adolf Hitler.
In an interview with the BBC, Mr Zelenskyy called Putin "an aggressor" and "a killer".
Kyiv is urging the US to do more to achieve a peace outcome with Russia.

Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Donald Trump's relationship with Russia's Vladimir Putin is comparable to being friends with Adolf Hitler as Kyiv grows increasingly frustrated at how the US is handling peace negotiations.

In an interview with the BBC in Kyiv, Mr Zelenskyy said it was "strange" for the US president to call Mr Putin a friend and would be similar to making the same comment about Hitler during World War II.
"It's the same that somebody say about Hitler during the Second World War that he's a good friend. No, he's not a friend."
Donald Trump's relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin has been questioned by Kyiv. ( AP: Matt Rourke/Alexei Nikolsky )
Mr Zelenskyy was speaking a week after Mr Trump had embraced the Russian president as a "friend" at a summit in China.
Days later Mr Trump posted a photo on his Truth Social platform of the pair shaking hands there and titled it "My Friend".
Mr Trump's relationship with Mr Zelenskyy has long been uneasy , most notably breaking down publicly in February 2025 when the US president confronted him in the Oval Office.
The pair have continued to clash more recently with the US president blaming Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries for high energy costs and threatening to cut off intelligence support.
Mr Zelenskyy has said Mr Trump's position is encouraging Russia to continue attacking Ukraine.
Speaking with the BBC, Mr Zelenskyy complained the US was not doing enough to negotiate peace with Russia and called on "real helpful allies, who can push Russia" to achieve an outcome.
"They have to pressure on the situation. The situation is when Russia is aggressor," he said.
"It's not about comfortable talks. It's about strong country who can pressure because this country (US) has power and respect."
It comes as US envoy Jared Kushner praised the Russian president "grandmaster of politics" and a "historic figure" who had "shown restraint" by agreeing to not use nuclear weapons against Ukraine.

Mr Kushner, Trump's son-in-law who is mediating Russia-Ukraine talks with envoy Steve Witkoff, said that after talking at length with Putin, he believed Putin wanted peace almost five years after Moscow's invasion.

Mr Putin "has agreed not to use nuclear weapons, which obviously is a big thing, and he's reassured us that that's not his intention", Kushner said on a podcast by German media group Axel Springer Creators.
Mr Kushner added: "What (Putin) is saying is peace, but I think it's always peace on what terms" as the talks have hit "a little bit of a deadlock" over the fate of Ukrainian territory.

Mr Zelenskyy and European leaders have criticised Mr Putin for what they describe as Moscow's refusal to compromise and persistence to press on with an invasion which has killed hundreds of thousands of troops and thousands of Ukrainian civilians.
According to Mr Kushner, the Kremlin wants a new relationship with Washington as Russia seeks to keep NATO away from its borders.

Mr Trump has said on social media he would like to see Putin "pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe, in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly".

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said the US was approaching peace talks with an understanding of the need to eliminate what Russia calls the "root causes" of the conflict, including "the creation of threats to Russia's security right on our borders".

Mr Zelenskyy has warned Ukraine's intelligence indicates that Moscow is "completing preparations for a new massive strike" which Kyiv says aims to deprive civilians of power and running water as the winter approaches.
Russian missile and drone attacks have battered Ukraine's power grid, killed civilians and choked the economy since the invasion.
"The Russians continue to target substations, overhead powerlines, and the entire power grid," Mr Zelenskyy said on social media.

Ukraine is pushing its allies to provide more air defence supplies as crews work to restore electricity in six Ukrainian regions after a Russian assault on Wednesday night involving ballistic missiles and 113 drones.
Ukraine has used its own long-range weapons to hit back at targets in Russia , and Russian vessels docked at a Libyan port in an attack which has caused alarm amongst some European leaders.

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: "C-295 facility represents work culture of New India," says PM Modi as he and Spanish PM inaugurate facility
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Vadodara (Gujarat) [ India ], October 28 (ANI): Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Monday inaugurated the TATA- Airbus aircraft assembly facility complex in Vadodara. The facility will manufacture C-295 aircraft at the TATA Advanced Systems Limited campus. PM Modi said that the C-295 facility represents the work culture of a new India . "Recently, we lost the country's great son Ratan Tata ji. If he had been among us today, he would have been happy, but wherever his soul is, he would be happy. This C-295 aircraft factory reflects the new work culture of New India ... When I was the Gujarat CM, it was decided to set up a factory in Vadodara to build train coaches. The factory was also prepared for production within a record time. Today, we are exporting the metro coaches manufactured in that factory to other countries. I am confident that in the future, the aircraft made in this factory will also be exported to other countries," PM Modi said. "Today the defence manufacturing ecosystem in India is touching new heights. If we had not taken concrete steps 10 years ago, it would have been impossible to reach this level today. At that time, no one could even imagine that there could be such large-scale defence manufacturing in India . But we decided to walk on the new path, set a new goal for ourselves. And today the result is before us," PM Modi added. The Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez underlined the importance of the new industrial site. Sanchez said, "Today we are not only officially inaugurating a cutting-edge industrial facility. Today we're also witnessing how an extraordinary project between two emblematic companies becomes a reality. Prime Minister Modi, this is another triumph of your vision. Your vision is to turn India into an industrial powerhouse and a magnet for investment and business. This partnership between Airbus and Tata will contribute to the progress of the India n aerospace industry and will open new doors for the arrival of other European companies." " Tata is probably the best exponent of India n industrial strength. Its products and services are present in virtually every country on the planet. Tata is a giant among giants. As for Airbus , it embodies the very essence of a united Europe. Committed to technological innovation and the creation of jobs and prosperity. For my country, for Spain , being an integral part of the Airbus consortium, defending the values it represents. Values on which the very idea of Europe is based on cooperation, modernity and progress," Sanchez added. During the inauguration of the TATA Aircraft Complex for manufacturing C-295 aircraft, Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran announced the facility's goals. "The final aircraft assembly complex for the first aircraft to be delivered is being set up here. I must commit to our Prime Minister that exactly two years from now we will deliver the first indigenously manufactured aircraft and we will request and we'll work with your office to block the date so that you can come and inaugurate the facility and receive the first product. The first 200 engineers from Tata Group are already in Spain going through the training that is required, and we have worked with 40 SME companies and we will be adding more companies to build the entire localisation that is required for the product," he said. This collaboration between Tata Advanced Systems Ltd. (TASL) and Airbus Spain will mark India 's first private sector final assembly line (FAL) for military aircraft, boosting the nation's aerospace capabilities. The plant, located at TASL's Vadodara campus, is part of India 's Rs 2.5 billion deal signed in 2021 to acquire 56 C-295 military transport aircraft from Airbus . Under the agreement, Airbus will deliver 16 aircraft directly from Spain , while the remaining 40 will be manufactured in India by TASL. This project will create a comprehensive ecosystem for aircraft development, covering assembly, testing, certification, and maintenance throughout the lifecycle of the aircraft. Major India n defence players like Bharat Electronics Ltd (BEL) and Bharat Dynamics Ltd (BDL), along with smaller enterprises, are also contributing to this project. The C-295 aircraft will strengthen India 's Air Force fleet with a modern and more reliable transport solution. Earlier in the day, PM Modi and Sanchez participated in a roadshow in Vadodara as they headed to inaugurate Tata Advanced Systems Ltd's facility. (ANI)

items.title: India to grow at 6.8 pc in FY25 and 6.6 pc in FY26: S&P Global Market Intelligence
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): India's growth, although moderating, remains strong with a forecasted average of 6.8 per cent for the fiscal year 2024-25 and 6.6 per cent for 2025-26, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence . Despite a slowdown in economic momentum due to weaker public-sector investment, the outlook for India's economy is buoyed by several positive factors. Easing inflation, favourable monsoon conditions, and increased government social spending are expected to boost household demand. Additionally, healthy corporate balance sheets are playing a vital role in supporting the recovery of private investment. S&P Global Market Intelligence has released its October Global Economic Forecast update, emphasizing a steady global economic expansion supported by policy stimulus, while acknowledging risks from geopolitical factors. The outlook highlights moderating inflation and easing monetary policies as key factors steering the global economy towards a "soft landing."

Ken Wattret, global economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence , remarked, "The global economy is on track for a soft landing, with inflation rates moderating and monetary policy easing becoming more widespread. Still, geopolitical developments have the capacity to dampen or even derail the expansion." Report forecasts an annual real GDP growth rate of 4.3 per cent in 2024 and 4.4 per cent in 2025 for the region excluding China and Japan. Aiding this growth is resilient domestic demand, as regional central banks adopt more accommodative monetary stances. The start of the US Federal Reserve's easing cycle in September is creating more room for interest rate cuts, prompting several central banks, including those in the Philippines, New Zealand, Hong Kong SAR, and Indonesia, to lower rates. S&P Global Market Intelligence underscores that while the global economic outlook remains positive, risks persist. Geopolitical tensions could potentially derail economic progress, especially in regions with heightened uncertainties. Nonetheless, policy measures aimed at stimulating growth, coupled with moderating inflation, are setting the stage for a sustained economic expansion. (ANI)

items.title: Asia's Largest Mindfulness India Summit 2024 Marks a New Era for Corporate Culture and Personal Well-being with the Inau
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel PNN Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: The Mindfulness India Summit 2024, an initiative by the Mindful Science Centre, presented by HSBC and supported by CII Leadership and HR Committee, successfully concluded its two-day event on October 17 and 18, 2024, establishing new benchmarks in corporate culture and personal well-being. With over 40 international and national experts addressing mindfulness, emotional intelligence, and neuroscience, the summit highlighted how these principles are essential in transforming leadership, enhancing employee engagement, and fostering sustainable well-being within organizations. The evolving workplace landscape, particularly the increasing role of AI, requires a renewed focus on human-centric leadership and emotional resilience. The summit provided a platform for forward-thinking leaders to explore how mindfulness can effectively bridge this gap, ensuring both corporate excellence and employee well-being . The summit featured MasterChef Sanjeev Kapoor as the Chief Guest, who shared how mindful leadership has played a pivotal role in building his culinary empire. Along with Chris Ruane, Ex MP British Parliament and Chair of Mindfulness Initiative UK, J N Behl and Global Holistic Health Guru Mickey Mehta, Kapoor also launched Manish Behl's new book "Observe - 101 Mindfulness Practices", a guide designed to make mindfulness accessible for both professionals and individuals in their everyday lives. Behl, a global mindfulness expert and founder of the Mindful Science Centre, shared, "With this book, I want to demystify mindfulness and make it accessible to everyone. Mindfulness is not a complex or distant concept, but a practical tool for reducing stress, improving focus, and fostering deeper connections in both personal and professional settings." The Mindfulness India Summit 2024 has successfully proven that mindfulness is no longer a luxury but a necessity in modern corporate structures. By adopting mindfulness practices, organizations are not only creating more compassionate work environments but are also enhancing their overall performance and sustainability in a world increasingly shaped by technological and emotional complexity. The 2 days also saw the launch of Mindfulness Impact Awards, to honor organizations and individuals who have integrated mindfulness into their corporate structures and personal lives. These awards reflect the growing recognition that workplace culture directly affects employee productivity, creativity, and overall well-being. Manish Behl, founder of the awards, explained, "Corporate success today goes beyond profit; it's about fostering environments where employees thrive mentally, emotionally, and physically. Our vision with these awards is to inspire a deeper integration of mindfulness in corporate cultures worldwide. By recognizing these pioneers, we hope these awards inspire companies and individuals to further integrate mindfulness into their environments, ultimately fostering happier, more productive workplaces, communities, and a more compassionate world." The awards were designed to acknowledge champions of mindfulness across categories, recognizing those who incorporate mindful practices to improve workplace culture, employee engagement, and societal impact. Winners ranged from corporate giants like Aditya Birla Group and Accenture to global educators and community leaders. items.title: Vagus nerve stimulation slows growth and spread of pancreatic cancer
paras: Facebook Threads X / Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Reddit Email Print Pancreatic cancer is typically very difficult to treat CENTRE JEAN-PERRIN/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY An electrical implant that stimulates the vagus nerve slowed the growth and spread of pancreatic tumours in mice. The approach seems to work by helping cancer -killing immune cells infiltrate tumours, enabling a treatment that doesn’t normally work for pancreatic cancer to become effective.

“It’s very exciting,” says Timothy Wang at Columbia University in New York, who wasn’t involved in the research. “It’s the first study I know where electrical manipulation has been used to treat tumours outside the brain.”

The intervention made the tumours susceptible to immunotherapy, which helps immune cells destroy cancer but usually fails against pancreatic tumours. “That could be very significant for patients,” says Wang. “Getting immunotherapy to work is the holy grail right now for pancreatic cancer. It’s thought to be key to long-term survival.”

One way to potentially make immunotherapy work is through electrical stimulation. This is already used to treat some kinds of brain cancer , such as glioblastoma. Now, Lu Gan at the Huazhong University of Science and Technology in China and their colleagues have tested it for pancreatic cancer. More than 500,000 people are diagnosed with pancreatic cancer a year, of whom only 13 per cent survive 5 years, making it one of the deadliest forms of cancer.

Prior research by Wang and his colleagues has also shown that blocking electrical signals in the vagus nerve , which connects the brain to other organs, increases the growth of pancreatic cancer in mice. To see whether stimulating the nerve has the reverse effect, Gan’s team developed an electrical device – roughly 1-centimetre long – that wraps around part of the oesophagus.
When activated by ultrasound waves, sent from outside the body, the device sends electrical signals along a branch of the vagus nerve that runs from the oesophagus to the pancreas.

To put it to the test, the researchers implanted the device, which wasn’t yet activated, into mice. Six days later, cancerous cells were injected into their pancreas. After tumours had formed, the team activated the device for 20 minutes a day in half the mice. It remained inactive in the remaining mice, acting as a control.

About two weeks later, the tumours in the control mice weighed about 230 milligrams, on average, compared with about 190 milligrams in the mice that received electrical stimulation – an almost 20 per cent difference. “I don’t think anyone would have predicted that big an effect,” says Wang.

The pancreatic cancer cells had also spread to more than 10 other parts of the control mice’s bodies, on average – about double the degree of spread that occurred among those that received electrical stimulation.

The more tumours spread, the deadlier they tend to be, however, the researchers didn’t measure the mice’s survival outcomes. This is probably because that would involve tracking a large number of mice over a longer period, and this was just a proof-of-concept study, says Wang. The researchers did find, however, that the device had no known short-term safety issues.

In another part of the experiment, the researchers found that the electrical stimulation seemed to boost the number of cancer-killing immune cells, called T-cells and natural killer cells, in the tumours. It also reduced the abundance of other kinds of immune cells, called MDSCs, which suppress T-cells.

Exactly how this occurred is unclear, but prior studies suggest that stimulating the vagus nerve increases the release of a neurotransmitter called acetylcholine , which can bind to receptors on the surface of immune and cancer cells, altering their behaviour, says Wang.

Finally, the team explored whether the approach could make pancreatic tumours respond to an immunotherapy drug, called anti-PD1, which activates T-cells but is usually ineffective against this type of cancer. “Pancreatic cancer is notorious for having an almost zero response to immunotherapy, and most believe that’s because pancreatic cancer has a tremendously fibrous structure, which stops immune cells getting in,” says Wang. If electrical stimulation allows T-cells to infiltrate the pancreas, immunotherapy stands a better chance, he says.
A cancer-killing virus has stopped pancreatic tumours from growing and spreading in three people in an initial safety trial, raising hopes that it may help to beat the deadly condition

The researchers found that anti-PD1 alone had no substantial effect on tumour growth in mice with pancreatic tumours. But combining it with electrical stimulation slowed tumour growth and stopped cancers spreading more than electrical stimulation alone.

This suggests this combination treatment could improve survival outcomes, says Wang. “Long-term survival in pancreatic cancer really does require T-cell immunity and getting immunotherapy to work.” It may be even more effective when combined with a non-immunotherapy drug, called daraxonrasib, that roughly doubles survival time in people with pancreatic cancer , says Wang.

Further research should first test whether the findings can be replicated in other mouse models of pancreatic cancer that better mimic what happens in people, for instance, by using mice that have been genetically engineered to develop pancreatic tumours, says Wang. These studies could also assess survival outcomes, he says. If successful, trials in people could start within the next couple of years, he says.

Every year, MIT Technology Review honors 35 of the world's brightest young scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors in our Innovators Under 35 list. And starting today, our 2027 competition is officially open for nominations.

He's also taking part in a clinical trial of new tech that allows him to move—and feel with—a prosthetic hand. Before the trial started, researchers scanned his brain to see how his missing left hand was represented in his brain. Will that change? items.title: Intel faced a choice: Give Trump 10% or face the consequences
paras: Corporate capitalism Intel faced a choice: Give Trump 10% or face the consequences Intel faced pressure to surrender a 10% stake to unlock billions in promised grants.

59 ... ... ... Credit: Intel Credit: Intel Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav The message from the Trump administration to one of the world’s leading semiconductor companies was clear: Give the US government a chunk of your company. Right now. Or else.

Do not make the “mistake of thinking that this is a negotiation,” Commerce Department lawyer David Shapiro told the chief financial officer of the Intel Corporation in August 2025, according to internal notes from a company call contained in a federal lawsuit. “The President is expecting to announce a deal on these terms on Friday.”

Shapiro acknowledged that “the Board could choose not to accept the offer,” according to a summary of his remarks prepared for Intel’s directors. But the Trump administration official “noted that rejection will have consequences that [Shapiro] cannot predict.”

Days later, the board gave the administration what it wanted . “It is my Great Honor to report that the United States of America now fully owns and controls 10% of INTEL,” Donald Trump posted to his social platform . “The United States paid nothing for these Shares, and the Shares are now valued at approximately $11 Billion Dollars. This is a great Deal for America.”

President Trump was similarly jubilant on Monday, announcing that he had “ convinced ” Nvidia’s board of directors to rehire chief executive Jensen Huang. The proclamation was a shock. But it wasn’t entirely without precedent.

Fifteen months earlier, the Trump administration had interfered with the leadership decisions at another major chipmaker, court documents allege. Then, as now, allegations swirled that the company’s CEO was too close to China. Then, as now, the Trump administration dealt itself into the company’s financial future.

It’s part of a broader shift within the government in general and the Commerce Department in particular, a former member of that department tells WIRED. Out are old metrics “like creating jobs or the US being more competitive or owning more of the market share,” this ex-Trump administration official says. When dealing with private companies, a single overriding concern is: “Are you going to give back to the government in cash?”

Documents unredacted as part of a shareholder’s lawsuit against Intel’s board show how far the administration has been willing to go to get what it wants. The lawsuit’s allegations were previously reported by WP Intelligence.

“The Board, operating under the shadow of the President’s threats,” the lawsuit alleges, “caved to the government’s extortion.” A second case, asking for internal records, was filed in April by the same shareholder, Richard Paisner, against Nvidia.

“It’s just straight-up coercion,” says Scott Lincicome, a vice president at the libertarian Cato Institute. “The company starts making decisions not based on what’s best for the company in the short or long term, what’s best for shareholders, but what’s best for politics and what the government is demanding.”

“That’s not what you want from any company,” he adds. “When you’re talking about the world’s most innovative companies and these kinds of bleeding-edge technologies that have not only huge economic implications but national security ones, then that’s a huge problem.”
Representatives for Intel declined to comment for this story. The White House, Commerce Department, and Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment.

The parallels between Nvidia’s government-assisted autogolpe and Intel’s alleged forced sale aren’t exact. In the Intel case, Trump all but accused the company’s boss of being compromised by Beijing; in the Nvidia situation, the president reportedly dismissed concerns from his own intelligence agencies about the executive’s connections to China. But both instances show a growing fusion of private enterprise and public office .

During the Biden administration, Intel won awards for up to $11 billion in government grants and contracts, much of it under the CHIPS Act, which was meant to help build semiconductor manufacturing and assembly plants in America and bolster domestic research.

At the time, there was some grumbling inside the Commerce Department, which administered the CHIPS and Science Act grants, about funding what was seen as a “failing incumbent” in the semiconductor space, says the former official. (Intel had, in recent years, fallen on hard times .) But by March 2025, Intel had received about $2.2 billion of the grants. That’s when President Trump told Congress that the CHIPS Act was “ a horrible, horrible thing .” The rest of Intel’s money was put on hold, tied to hitting certain milestones, while the administration said it was renegotiating the deals.

The same month Lip-Bu Tan was hired as Intel’s new CEO. Soon after, his ties to China made him a Trump target, when Reuters reported that Tan had invested in “hundreds of Chinese tech firms,” some with connections to Beijing’s military. Tan’s former firm, Cadence Design Systems, pleaded guilty to violating US sanctions by selling semiconductor designs to a restricted Chinese military university, and agreed to pay more than $140 million in fines. Tan was never personally charged, but the violations happened while he was the CEO.

Two weeks later, the president was watching Maria Bartiromo’s show on the Fox Business Network. It mentioned a letter a senator had sent Intel about the China ties. Trump posted , “The CEO of INTEL is highly CONFLICTED and must resign, immediately. There is no other solution to this problem.”
Tan went to the Oval Office on August 11 to see if there was, in fact, another solution. He got 40 minutes with the president, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

Tan claimed his experience in China was a strength, not a detriment. According to the book Regime Change , Tan argued that there was no way he could’ve known about every one of the deals his many companies made; Trump, who had his own sprawling business empire, surely knew what that was like. Tan promised to give up his holdings in China, according to a letter Tan shared with Intel’s board, and put any proceeds into a blind trust.

“The primary goal was to eliminate any worries about Lip-Bu himself, his Cadence background, and his investments with China,” according to a source with knowledge of the matter. But there were major financial concerns for Intel, too. “We had declining revenues and needed money.”

Neither Tan’s letter, excerpted in the complaint, nor Trump’s social media posts praising the CEO after the meeting mentioned anything about giving the government a chunk of the company. Yet Trump later insisted that a deal had been cooked up right then and there. “He came in, he saw me, we talked for a while. I liked him a lot, I thought he was very good,” the president told The Wall Street Journal. “I said, ‘You know what? I think the United States should be given 10% of Intel.’ And he said, ‘I would consider that.’”

According to the court filing’s review of Intel’s internal documents, Shapiro—a former partner at the New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz—made a verbal offer on August 18. Ultimately, in exchange for the cut of Intel, the Trump administration would free up the $8.9 billion US government grants that it had already won. They wanted about a tenth of the company’s stock for free, in exchange for Washington keeping the commitment it had already made.

Then came the call in which Shapiro insisted there was no room for negotiation. “The board needs to consider,” he said, according to Intel’s summary of his remarks included in the court documents, the “benefits of having a friend in this administration and what the administration can do to help Intel (including with customers).”

Intel’s board met, and decided they hated the deal. “The economic terms that had been proposed [by] the Administration were not, in their current form, attractive to the company,” minutes of the meeting, reprinted in the lawsuit, noted.

But they went ahead with it anyway. Paisner’s lawyers say in the court documents the board took the offer thrust forward by the administration. Intel’s attorneys disagree, arguing in their motion to dismiss that there was some back-and-forth deal-making, and it made the agreement more favorable to the company. The grants became “immediately available” while “strategically aligning the interests of Intel’s stockholders and the US Government.”

On August 25, Lutnick released a video with Tan, sitting side-by-side on cushioned chairs. “I really look forward to have the US government be my shareholder,” Tan turned to Lutnick and said. “And we can work together and make Intel great again.”
Inside the company, the video was “a surprise to everyone,” according to a source with direct knowledge of the matter. Some employees joked that it was reminiscent of a “hostage video.”

Not long after that, Nvidia—led by Tan’s friend Jensen Huang—made a $5 billion investment in Intel. “I love seeing their stock price go up, making the USA RICHER, AND RICHER,” Trump posted . “Who would not want to make deals like that?”

Deals, plural. On the day Tan was hauled to the Oval Office, Trump announced that his administration had been negotiating separately with Huang . The Nvidia leader was beyond eager to sell more of his semiconductors to China. “And I said, if I’m going to do that, I want you to pay us as a country something,’” Trump said. They settled on 15 percent of all sales of the H20 model chip. Months after that, they cut a second deal: a 25 percent bounty on sales of Nvidia’s even-more advanced H200 chips.

In their lawsuit against Nvidia, Paisner’s attorneys argue the surcharges amount to “unlawful taxes,” and that the board’s “decisions to enter into such agreements are the product of mismanagement and breaches of fiduciary duty.”

In court, NVIDIA’s lawyers insisted that the company “did not enter into any illegal ‘agreement’ with the government but instead engaged with the government and stated that it would comply with federal regulations.” Moreover, the attorneys say Paisner is trying to make a political point, rather than a legal one. “When asked about his purpose in bringing this action,” they write, “Paisner was candid: ‘It’s to make a public point of how NVIDIA conducts itself.’”

The attorneys wrote this in May, months before Nvidia’s and Huang’s recent drama. Last week, board chair Harvey Jones said on the company’s quarterly earnings call that it did “ not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO ,” citing his “disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms.” (Not to mention mounting evidence that the company’s most sophisticated chips were making their way to China, in violation of US law.) But, according to The New York Times, after days of pressure from top administration officials, the company and the government essentially struck a deal Sunday night to reinstate Huang.

“Don’t think for a second that politics ever play a role in this company, not even a little bit,” Huang said during his first company-wide meeting after rejoining the company, WIRED reported . “We are the most apolitical company. I don’t love that we talk about politics here. Take it home. I love that we talk about work here.”

items.title: Tim Henman picks who will be British number one over Jack Draper by the end of 2027
paras: Jack Draper has suffered more than most with injury concerns throughout 2026. The hope is that 2027 can be the year when he gets things on track.

In all honesty, it cannot be much worse than the past 11 months, which have seen the Brit miss all four Grand Slams and an estimated total of six months of action. At one stage, the 24-year-old was fourth in the world and a US Open semi-finalist, having just won Indian Wells.

The hope is that Jack Draper can find some semblance of that form in the new season, having already begun his training. Speaking on the Sky Sports Review, a handful of their biggest pundits offered their thoughts on the future of British tennis. Currently, Arthur Fery and Sonay Kartal are occupying the number one spots on the ATP and WTA Tours, but the general consensus seems to be that this will all change in 2027.

items.title: David Ferrer suggests what Great Britain are the best in the world at ahead of Davis Cup semi-final
paras: David Ferrer is wary of the threat that Great Britain will pose to his Spanish team ahead of their Davis Cup semi-final.

Ferrer did not even need Carlos Alcaraz for Spain’s quarter-final tie against Austria, as the seven-time Grand Slam champion was rested, while Rafael Jodar and Daniel Merida both took care of their respective singles matches.

Great Britain have not been in the semi-finals of the Davis Cup since 2019, when they were beaten by Spain. Ferrer was not Spain’s captain at the time, and he has praised the current British players after watching them beat Germany. Ferrer was asked about the Great Britain team in his press conference after beating Austria, as he praised the way Norrie played in the third set in particular of his singles win against Struff.

items.title: Jakub Mensik’s 2026 Season Recap: Another Step Towards the Elite
paras: The Czech began the season with an early title in Auckland, reached his first Grand Slam semifinal at Roland Garros and achieved a career-high ranking of World No. Although consistency at the biggest tournaments remained a work in progress, his performances against established names demonstrated that he is increasingly capable of competing with the best.

Mensik made an excellent start to the season by capturing the Auckland title. He defeated Sebastian Baez 6-3 7-6 in the final, saving three consecutive set points in the second-set tiebreak to secure his second ATP Tour singles title.

He also became the youngest Auckland champion since Juan Martin del Potro in 2009. He carried that momentum into the Australian Open, reaching the fourth round for the first time, and then delivered further encouraging performances in Doha, where he defeated Jannik Sinner before reaching the semifinals.

items.title: Ryan Harrison claims Henry Patten and Neal Skupski aren’t telling the truth about how they became doubles partners
paras: Henry Patten and Neal Skupski will join forces in 2027, leaving their former teammates, Harri Heliovaara and Christian Harrison, behind. The move was shocking, to say the least.
Patten split from Heliovaara days after they lifted the year-end number one trophy together in Turin. Heliovaara said he felt ‘heavy disappointment’ after the Briton delivered the news.

Patten and Skupski have both shared their side of the story during an appearance on ‘ 5 Live Sport ‘. I told him this opportunity does not come along very often to play with another Brit who is world number one and to be able to play Davis Cup and the Olympics in the future. I don’t know if he quite believed me that we hadn’t spoken beforehand, but that two or three hours after the match we had decided, and I’m very happy and comfortable with my decision,” said Skupski.

items.title: November 27, 2011: The day Roger Federer won a then-record sixth ATP Finals title
paras: Every day, Tennis Majors takes you back to one of the biggest moments in tennis history. On November 27, 2011, Roger Federer and Jo-Wilfried Tsonga clashed for the eighth time in the season

On this day, November 27 in 2011, Roger Federer defeated Jo-Wilfried Tsonga (6-3, 6-7, 6-3) to claim a record sixth crown in the ATP Finals in London. After he finished 1998 as world No 1 in juniors, Federer performed well in his first professional matches: in his five first main tour appearances in 1998-1999, he reached the quarter-finals three times, in Toulouse, Marseille and Rotterdam.

His incredible game amazed the world tennis and soon, he was proclaimed as a likely future world No 1. The Swiss, very emotional during his first years on the tour, eventually mastered his nerves in 2003, when he claimed his first major title at Wimbledon (defeating Mark Philippoussis in the final, 7-6, 6-2, 7-6).
items.impact: A few months later, after triumphing at the Australian Open (defeating Marat Safin in the final, 7-6, 6-4, 6-3), he became world No 1 on February 2, 2004, and he held that spot without a break for 237 weeks.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
